config.title: Implement RequireOnlyOne type

intro.title: Implement RequireOnlyOne type
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom TypeScript utility type called `RequireOnlyOne`. This type will enforce that exactly one property from a set of keys is required in an object, while all others are optional. You will learn to use TypeScript's mapped types, conditional types, and the `Exclude` utility to create this constraint. By the end, you'll understand how to design flexible type definitions that improve code safety and clarity. This exercise will strengthen your skills in advanced TypeScript type manipulation.
intro.usecase: The RequireOnlyOne type is essential in UI components where a user must select exactly one option from a set of mutually exclusive properties. For example, in a dashboard settings panel, a chart configuration might allow either a custom data source URL or an uploaded file, but not both simultaneously. Similarly, a form for creating a notification could accept either a specific date-time or a relative time offset, ensuring the backend receives a single, unambiguous value. This pattern prevents invalid states and clarifies component APIs in complex applications like data visualizations or user preference modals.

objectives: Construct a generic type that excludes all but one property from a union of keys.
Apply conditional types to enforce a single required property from a set.
Implement the RequireOnlyOne utility type using TypeScript's built-in mapped types.
Integrate the RequireOnlyOne type into a function signature to validate parameters.
Manipulate existing object types to restrict property combinations.
Configure a type alias that ensures exactly one property is present from a specified list.
Initialize a variable with a type that requires only one property from multiple options.

steps.title: Import TypeScript utilities
steps.instruction: Import the TypeScript utility types you'll need for creating custom types. Use a single import statement to bring in `Partial`, `Required`, `Pick`, and `Omit` from 'typescript'.
steps.hint: TypeScript provides built-in utility types that you can import from the 'typescript' module. Use the syntax: `import { ... } from 'typescript';`
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple utilities
import { Partial, Required, Pick, Omit } from 'typescript';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary TypeScript utility types imported and ready to use in your custom type implementations.
successCriteria: The import statement includes `Partial`, `Required`, `Pick`, and `Omit` from 'typescript'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing all four utility types: `Partial`, `Required`, `Pick`, and `Omit` from 'typescript'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement doesn't match what's needed. Remember to import `Partial`, `Required`, `Pick`, and `Omit` from 'typescript' in a single import statement.

steps.title: Create a helper type to exclude keys
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript helper type named 'ExcludeOne' that takes two generic parameters: T (an object type) and K (a key of T). It should create a new type where all properties of T are optional, and the property K is excluded.
steps.hint: Use mapped types with 'keyof T' and a conditional type to check if each key equals K. If it does, exclude it (use 'never'), otherwise make it optional with '?'.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a helper type that can create a version of any object type with one specific property excluded and all others optional.
successCriteria: The ExcludeOne type is defined with two generic parameters T and K extends keyof T, uses mapped types with conditional types, and correctly excludes property K while making other properties optional.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your type definition. Make sure: 1) It has two generic parameters T and K extends keyof T, 2) It uses a mapped type over keyof T, 3) It uses a conditional type to exclude property K (map to 'never'), 4) Other properties should be optional.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ExcludeOne type isn't defined correctly. Remember: You need to create a type that takes an object type T and a key K, then produces a new type where property K is excluded and all other properties are optional.

steps.title: Define the RequireOnlyOne type
steps.instruction: Create a generic type called RequireOnlyOne<T> that uses mapped types and unions to require exactly one property from the provided type T.
steps.hint: Use a mapped type to create a union where each property is required and all others are optional with never type.
steps.expectedOutcome: The RequireOnlyOne<T> type will be defined and ready to use with BaseProps.
successCriteria: RequireOnlyOne type is defined as a generic type
Type uses mapped types and unions
Type properly requires exactly one property from the input type
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your type is generic (RequireOnlyOne<T>) and uses mapped types to create a union of all possible single-property requirements.
